findings.text: Creation routine for the virtual dual 8259 facility allocates per virtual machine state, prepares chip masks and back links, publishes three programmed input output windows, and on any bus conflict unwinds earlier windows and frees state while reporting the failure.

Creation routine for the virtual input output APIC allocates per virtual machine state, prepares its lock and deferred work and notifier set, applies reset defaults, publishes a memory mapped window, and on conflict detaches and frees state while reporting the failure.

Routing entry injection for one IOAPIC pin validates the pin range, folds the caller level with other sources for that pin, forwards the resulting level to the core pin logic, and returns its coalesced or delivered indication.

Scan helpers let a virtual CPU refresh which vectors need end of interrupt interception after routing or masking changes, including recording the largest stale pending vector when the CPU is no longer a target.

Small query helpers report whether a chip pin has an acknowledgement notifier, whether a resampler consumed a pending level interrupt, whether accelerated APIC virtualization is currently uninhibited, and restore one real time clock tracking slot under lock.

Three programmed input output operation tables expose master slave and edge level control windows, each pairing a one byte read wrapper with a matching write wrapper that resolves the enclosing chip state and delegates to shared logic.

One memory mapped operation table exposes the IOAPIC selector and window registers, pairing a length tolerant read path with a size checked write path that both filter by base range and serialize with the chip lock.

Programmed input output dispatch directs the two low master addresses to the first chip, the two low slave addresses to the second chip, and the two edge control addresses split by parity across chips, rejecting other addresses and requiring single byte transfers.

Port reads honor a one shot poll mode that consumes the pending flag, otherwise even addresses return either service or request state according to a selector flag while odd addresses return the mask state.

Poll completion clears the delivered request and service indications, clears the cascade linkage in the master when servicing through the slave window, refreshes the output, and encodes presence with the top bit set versus a small fixed value for absence.
Edge level control writes are constrained by a per chip mask so only permitted lines are retained, and reads return the retained value unchanged.

Indirect reads expose a version register combining pin count and version identity, identifier registers exposing the low nibble at the top byte, and redirection entries as paired low and high halves with out of range selectors yielding all ones.

Indirect writes ignore version, update only the identifier nibble from the top byte, update one half of a redirection entry while preserving delivery and remote state, clear remote indication for edge mode, and announce mask transitions to registered listeners.

Core pin assertion clears pending state on deassertion, else for edge mode clears the delivered marker and reports coalesced when pending state did not change, while a real time clock pin additionally reports coalesced when end of interrupt tracking shows unfinished work.
Unmasking a level pin with pending and unacknowledged state first offers the pending work to a resampler to drop stale requests, falling back to immediate delivery only when no resampler accepts.

Reset masks every redirection entry, clears pending and delivered sets and selector and identifier and base to defaults, cancels deferred end of interrupt work synchronously, and reinitializes real time clock tracking and end of interrupt history.

Memory mapped accesses outside the configured window are refused, the low byte of the address selects selector versus window versus ignore, selector writes retain only the low byte, and read results are truncated to the requested transfer width.
Deferred end of interrupt work rescans all pins and reissues delivery only for level entries that remain pending and lack remote acknowledgement.
Bulk reinjection resets real time clock tracking, reasserts every pin marked in the supplied pending set as asserted with line status true, then restores tracking for all virtual CPUs.

Scan coverage includes every level entry plus any pin with an acknowledgement notifier plus the real time clock pin, always using the entry destination and vector to mark handled vectors or stale pending state.
Destination bitmap construction prefers an accelerated map lookup when available and otherwise scans all present CPUs for destination match, setting the caller bitmap for each selected CPU index.
Fixed delivery with changed destination requests a scan on the union of old and new target sets, while all other redirection changes request a global scan.
Lazy end of interrupt refresh on edge assertion under acceleration walks virtual CPUs to find the first destination without pending state and applies the real time clock completion for that vector.
Log prefix for this file combines the module name with the supplied format text.
All programmed input output and edge control reads and writes hold the virtual PIC spin protection across the underlying port operation, with thin wrappers adding no additional synchronization.
All IOAPIC indirect, memory mapped, pin injection, scan, deferred work, and real time clock restore paths hold the IOAPIC spin protection across state inspection and mutation.
Bus publication and rollback for both PIC and IOAPIC creation hold the virtual machine slots mutex, released before publishing success to the architecture state.
Acknowledgement notifier and resampler list walks hold the interrupt source read side section, and destination bitmap fast path holds the read side section for the APIC map.

Observed PIC state comprises per chip request mask service edge control and mask plus poll and selector flags and a back link to shared state, with shared state holding the lock virtual machine link and three bus devices.

Observed IOAPIC state comprises base address selector identifier pending and delivered sets redirection table per pin line state end of interrupt history real time clock tracking mask notifier set deferred work device node lock and virtual machine link.

Redirection entries behave as sixty four bit values with separately addressable low and high halves, carrying vector delivery destination trigger mask and remote acknowledgement fields with only some fields writable.
PIC poll mode is a one shot state where a set flag diverts the next read to delivery and clears itself, otherwise reads follow the selector and mask path without side effects.

Redirection update moves from selector validation through half update and preservation to optional notifier and delivery actions, ending with either targeted or global scan requests depending on delivery type and destination stability.

Level pin lifecycle moves from asserted pending to delivered with remote acknowledgement to end of interrupt completion, with deferred work and unmask handling reissuing delivery when pending persists without remote acknowledgement.
Non single byte PIC transfers log and either ignore the write or return zeroes on read, while unsupported addresses and out of range IOAPIC windows report not supported without state change.

Out of range pin injection warns once and fails, out of range redirection selectors are ignored or read as all ones with speculative hardening, and unsupported memory mapped lengths warn without mutating state.

Stale pending state after masked level handling can cause an extra delivery without a resampler present, and coalesced edge or real time clock assertions intentionally suppress duplicate delivery and are reported distinctly.
PIC master window base is 0x20 length 2, slave base is 0xa0 length 2, edge control base is 0x4d0 length 2, master edge mask is 0xf8 and slave edge mask is 0xde, transfers must be length 1.
Poll presence sets the top bit corresponding to 0x80, absence yields the fixed value 0x07.
IOAPIC memory mapped transfers accept widths 1 2 4 and 8 bytes, unsupported widths warn, register selection uses the low 8 bits of address and selector stores only its low 8 bits.

Successive interrupt bound is 10000, redirection index derives from selector minus 0x10 halved, odd selectors read the high half, version places pin count minus one in bits 16 to 23 with version in low byte and identifier places low nibble in bits 24 to 31.
